name: Maadai
title: Israelite who sent away his foreign wife
summary: Maadai was one of the descendants of Bani who lived in the period after the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the Israelites who had taken foreign (non-Jewish) wives and agreed to send them away as part of Ezra's religious reforms to preserve the purity of the people.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the descendants of Bani
keyEvents.description: Maadai is listed among the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign wives in violation of God's law.

keyEvents.title: Acknowledgment of sin
keyEvents.description: Maadai was among those who acknowledged that taking foreign wives was a transgression against the Lord, and he committed to correcting the error.

keyEvents.title: Promise to send away the foreign wives
keyEvents.description: As part of the collective covenant led by Ezra, Maadai and the others promised to send away their foreign wives and their children.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reforms and the assembly
keyEvents.description: Ezra gathered all the people in Jerusalem to address the issue of mixed marriages, and Maadai was among those who responded to the call.

keyEvents.title: List of the Guilty
keyEvents.description: Maadai is recorded by name in the official list of men who had taken foreign wives, as a testimony that he too participated in this sin and the subsequent repentance.
